paper_id: Requirements-Driven Dynamic Adaptation to Mitigate Runtime Uncertainties for Self-Adaptive Systems
title: Requirements-Driven Dynamic Adaptation to Mitigate Runtime Uncertainties for Self-Adaptive Systems
motivation: In self-adaptive systems, runtime changes cannot be exhaustively anticipated at design time, so dynamic adaptation mechanisms must be provided at requirements phase
problem_framing: Runtime uncertainty as context uncertainty (environment) and components uncertainty (system itself); adaptation must be derived from requirements model specifications
key_insight: Treat requirements model as runtime entity that evolves with MAPE loop; parametric adaptation handles context uncertainty violations, structural adaptation handles components uncertainty violations
method_signature: REDAPT uses Adaptive Goal Model (AGM) with temporal logic grammar to derive MAPE-based adaptation mechanism algorithms from requirements specifications
evaluation_criteria: Simulation experiments on Highway-Rail Control System demonstrating parametric adaptation for NFR and functional requirements satisfaction
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: For the third case in NFR violation experiment, 'further tuning is needed' — one adaptive goal could not be satisfied with current parameter adjustments
evidence_for_taste: AGM as runtime entity, which can evolve
thinking_moves: 把运行时不确定性严格区分为context uncertainty和components uncertainty两类
把goal model扩展为runtime entity，在运行时动态演化
用temporal logic grammar形式化AGM元素以弥合需求模型与adaptation mechanisms之间的gap
通过violation分类匹配对应的adaptation mechanism algorithm (parametric vs structural)
在实验中使用utility function对NFR satisfaction degree进行量化验证
extraction_notes: Paper is from arXiv preprint without traditional venue. Zhi Jin listed as co-author with email; role unclear (not first or corresponding). Some algorithm details appear truncated in figures. NFR experiment shows one case where adaptation failed.
